#001

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00001
High Custom + axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A High - detected by both engines Link recommendation V4
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .facebook | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="https://www.facebook.com/duadministration" class="facebook" target="_blank"><img src="https://www.du.ac.bd/fontView/social_link/fb.png" style="padding-right: 10px"></a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

Custom scanner evidence

Link has no accessible name. Add meaningful link text, aria-label, or image alt text.

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Context-Aware Link Recommendation

Destination / action: https://www.facebook.com/duadministration

Suggested accessible name:
“Facebook page”

Recommended action: Provide the link with an accessible name describing its destination or function. Preserve meaningful visible content and avoid redundant wording.

Why this suggestion was made: The destination/function can be derived from explicit link or icon evidence without guessing visual meaning.

Issue: missing accessible name Decision: social destination Context confidence: high Evidence: explicit Facebook destination URL

Evidence used: https://www.facebook.com/duadministration

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This candidate was generated by deterministic destination and context rules. Confidence describes the strength of the available evidence and does not establish WCAG conformance.

Link V4 Suggested HTML 

<a aria-label="Facebook page" class="facebook" href="https://www.facebook.com/duadministration" target="_blank"><img src="https://www.du.ac.bd/fontView/social_link/fb.png" style="padding-right: 10px"/></a>

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Custom scanner evidence

axe description

Medium Custom Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) Level A Contextual/manual review Context-aware recommendation Link recommendation V4
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Text such as 'Read More', 'More', or 'Click Here' may not clearly identify the link destination when encountered outside its visual context.

Location

DOM selector: div.col-md-4:nth-of-type(2) > div.top-author:nth-of-type(2) > div.author-items:nth-of-type(1) > div.item:nth-of-type(1) > div.info > ul > li:nth-of-type(2) > a.btn.circle | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a class="btn circle btn-dark border btn-sm text-center" href="https://www.du.ac.bd/du_post_details/notice/28421" target="_blank"> <i class="fas fa-plus" style="color: #002147"></i> Read More</a>

Custom scanner evidence

Link text is generic and does not clearly identify the destination.

Recommended change

Prefer descriptive link text that communicates the destination or purpose. If generic wording is retained, verify that programmatically determined context makes the purpose clear.

Context-Aware Recommendation

আরও পড়ুন: পরিজন উপবৃত্তি বিজ্ঞপ্তি

Why this suggestion was made: The nearby nearby heading provides a specific description of the destination, so it can be used to make the generic link purpose clearer.

Evidence: nearby heading Context confidence: high Language: bn Decision: LINK_CONTEXT_AVAILABLE

Recommended action: replace or expand accessible link name

Human verification: Required before implementation.

This recommendation was generated by the proposed deterministic contextual decision engine. Context confidence describes the strength of the extracted contextual evidence, not WCAG conformance certainty.

#115

Button does not have a discernible accessible name

button-name  •  UF-00115
Critical axe Controls WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Users of assistive technology may encounter a button without knowing its purpose.

Location

DOM selector: .cloned.owl-item:nth-child(1) > .item > .aos-init.thumb[data-aos="fade-up-right"] > .thumb > iframe[height="180"] .ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar | Ownership: third_party_embed | Actionability: third_party_controlled

Affected HTML 

<button class="ytmVideoInfoLink ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar"><img class="ytCoreImageHost ytmVideoInfoChannelLogo ytCoreImageFillParentHeight ytCoreImageFillParentWidth ytCoreImageContentModeScaleAspectFill" alt="thumbnail-image" style="background-color: transparent;"></button>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have inner text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute
  Element does not have an implicit (wrapped) <label>
  Element does not have an explicit <label>
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

axe description

Ensure buttons have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible button text or an appropriate accessible name such as aria-label when the control is icon-only.

Suggested code pattern 

<button aria-label="Describe button action" class="ytmVideoInfoLink ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar"><img alt="thumbnail-image" class="ytCoreImageHost ytmVideoInfoChannelLogo ytCoreImageFillParentHeight ytCoreImageFillParentWidth ytCoreImageContentModeScaleAspectFill" style="background-color: transparent;"/></button>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the computed accessible name after the change.
Third-party content

#125

Embedded frame does not have an accessible name

frame-title  •  UF-00125
High axe Frames WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Users may not know what content an iframe contains when it has no descriptive accessible name.

Location

DOM selector: .cloned.owl-item:nth-child(1) > .item > .aos-init.thumb[data-aos="fade-up-right"] > .thumb > iframe[height="180"] | Ownership: first_party_integration | Actionability: directly_fixable

Affected HTML 

<iframe width="100%" height="180" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/E_g7OXHop74" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element has no title attribute
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

axe description

Ensure <iframe> and <frame> elements have an accessible name

Recommended change

Add a concise title attribute to the iframe describing the embedded content.

Suggested code pattern 

<iframe allowfullscreen="" frameborder="0" height="180" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/E_g7OXHop74" title="Describe embedded content" width="100%"></iframe>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

The title should accurately describe the actual embedded content.

Reference

region  •  UF-00188
Medium axe Landmarks WCAG Best practice / structural navigation Level Best practice Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Landmarks can help assistive-technology users navigate major areas of a page efficiently.

Location

DOM selector: .active.owl-item:nth-child(6) > .item > .aos-init.thumb[data-aos="fade-up-right"] > .thumb > iframe[height="180"] .quick-actions-wrapper | Ownership: third_party_embed | Actionability: third_party_controlled

Affected HTML 

<div class="quick-actions-wrapper">

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Some page content is not contained by landmarks

axe description

Ensure all page content is contained by landmarks

Recommended change

Review whether the content belongs inside an appropriate semantic landmark such as <main>, <nav>, <header>, <footer>, or another labelled region.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Adding landmarks blindly can create excessive or incorrect landmark structure.
Third-party content

This finding appears inside an embedded third-party document. The website owner may not directly control the internal markup. Review the embed configuration, integration, provider options, or whether a more accessible alternative is available.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

Review axe — manual review Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Manual review required
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: .row:nth-child(1) > .col-md-4:nth-child(1) > table > tbody > tr:nth-child(1) > td[colspan="2"] > strong | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<strong>জাতীয় শুদ্ধাচার কৌশল</strong>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element's background color could not be determined because it's partially obscured by another element

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

Methodology note: Automated accessibility testing can identify many important problems, but it cannot establish complete WCAG conformance. Context-dependent and incomplete findings require human review. Context-aware recommendations are produced by deterministic rules using extracted local page context and should be verified before implementation. VLM-assisted image recommendations use visual-semantic evidence from a local vision-language model, followed by deterministic accessibility guardrails. They remain human-review recommendations rather than automatic WCAG conformance decisions.
